concept.title: MathML
concept.shortdesc: With MathML you write mathematical formulas in XML. CSSMedia lays them out with the rules of the language and draws them as vector graphics and text in the PDF. This chapter explains how to put a formula in your document, how to build the common structures and how to style them. The MathML reference at the end lists the properties, elements and attributes.

conbody.p: A MathML formula describes the structure of an expression, not its look. A fraction is a mfrac with a numerator and a denominator, and CSSMedia decides where the bar goes, how big the parts are and how far apart. For example, the equation x squared plus y squared equals z squared is part of this line of text, and its baseline is the baseline of the text.
MathML elements belong to a namespace, so a formula starts with a math element that declares it:
You can put a formula in two places:

ul.li: In your own XML, at the place where it must appear. A math element in the MathML namespace is part of the text that surrounds it.
In a file of its own, which an element of your XML shows as an image. The file holds one math element, and CSSMedia knows it is a formula from that element, not from the name of the file.

conbody.p: Put a formula in your document explains both. The formulas in this chapter are files of the second kind, and each one is shown with the XML that makes it.
These are the elements that CSSMedia lays out:

row.entry: Element
What it does
Holds a formula.
mi, mn, mo, mtext, ms, mspace
Hold the identifiers, numbers, operators, text, strings and spaces of the formula.
mrow, mstyle, mpadded, mphantom, merror
Group other elements, change their style, adjust the space around them, hide them or mark them as an error.
mfrac, msqrt, mroot, mfenced, menclose
Make fractions, roots, fences and enclosures.
msub, msup, msubsup, mmultiscripts, munder, mover, munderover
Put scripts, limits and accents around a base.
mtable, mtr, mtd
Make tables and matrices.
mstack, mlongdiv, msgroup, msrow, mscarries, mscarry, msline
Stack numbers for elementary arithmetic and long division.
semantics, annotation, annotation-xml, maction
Add other representations of a formula. CSSMedia draws the first child of semantics, and the child of maction that selection chooses.
Shows an image where a character would go.
Makes a link. CSSMedia also makes a link of any MathML element that has an href attribute.
cn, ci, csymbol, cs, apply, bind, bvar, set, list, vector, matrix, piecewise, the operator elements such as plus and sin, and the other elements of Content MathML
Describe what a formula means, and CSSMedia draws the usual notation for it.

conbody.p: An element of the MathML namespace that is not in this list is laid out as an mrow.
The topics of this chapter explain how to do each of these things:

ul.li: Put a formula in your document shows where a formula goes, how it gets its font and how it is linked.
Build the structures of a formula shows each presentation element.
Write a formula with Content MathML shows the elements that describe meaning.
Break a long formula into lines shows how a wide formula is broken, scaled, elided or cut.
Style a formula shows the attributes, the CSS rules, the math properties, the generated content and the equation numbers.

conbody.note: A formula is drawn with a font that has a MATH table: the data that tells a layout engine how high to raise a superscript, how thick a fraction bar is and which glyphs build a tall bracket. Choose that font in your style sheet, as Put a formula in your document shows.
